{"file_path":"<path>","content":"# File-type filtering in ripgrep

File-type filtering (`-t/--type`, `-T/--type-not`, `--type-add`, `--type-clear`,
`--type-list`) is implemented in the `ignore` crate, not in `ripgrep` itself.
Everything lives in `crates/ignore/src/types.rs`, with the built-in type list
in `crates/ignore/src/default_types.rs`. The `core` crate (the `rg` binary)
only parses flags into a small intermediate representation and hands them to
`ignore::types::TypesBuilder`.

## Representation

A single named type is a `FileTypeDef { name: String, globs: Vec<String> }`
(`crates/ignore/src/types.rs:146`). There is no separate AST for glob syntax —
each glob is stored as its original string and only compiled when the matcher
is built.

The built matcher is `Types`:

```rust
pub struct Types {
    defs: Vec<FileTypeDef>,
    selections: Vec<Selection<FileTypeDef>>,
    has_selected: bool,
    glob_to_selection: Vec<(usize, usize)>,
    set: GlobSet,
    matches: Arc<Pool<Vec<usize>>>,
}
```

`Selection<T>` is `Select(String, T) | Negate(String, T)` — it records both
*which* type a `-t`/`-T` flag referred to and *whether* it was a positive or
negative selection. `set` is a single `globset::GlobSet` containing every glob
from every selected/negated type, built with `literal_separator(true)`.
`glob_to_selection` maps each glob's index in that set back to `(index into
selections, index into that def's globs)`, which is how a match is traced
back to the `FileTypeDef` that caused it. `matches` is a `Pool` of reusable
scratch `Vec<usize>` buffers so `Types::matched` can call
`GlobSet::matches_into` without allocating per path (matching is meant to run
once per directory entry).

## Building a matcher

`TypesBuilder` (`types.rs:305`) accumulates raw definitions in a
`HashMap<String, FileTypeDef>` plus an ordered `Vec<Selection<()>>` of
selections/negations (order matters — see below). Key methods:

- `add(name, glob)` / `add_def("name:glob")` — append a glob to a type. Names
  must be all-alphanumeric and not `"all"`, or `Error::InvalidDefinition` /
  the check in `add()` rejects it.
- `add_def("name:include:other1,other2")` — the 3-part form copies the globs
  of already-defined types into a new type. It fails fast (before mutating
  anything) if any referenced type doesn't exist yet, so `add_def` is
  effectively atomic.
- `select(name)` / `negate(name)` — push a `Selection::Select`/`Negate`. The
  special name `"all"` expands to every type name currently in the map at
  call time (`select`/`negate` iterate `self.types.keys()`), not every type
  that will ever exist — so `--type-add` after `--type=all` still adds to the
  match set (globs are appended and then swept up regardless of when `all`
  was expanded relative to `build()`), but a type name added *after*
  `select("all")` was called and *before* another `select`/`negate` is fine
  because expansion happens at build time via the stored selections... check
  this against `build()`: `all` is expanded immediately inside `select`,
  against whatever `self.types` contains *at that call*. Order of
  `--type-add` vs `--type=all` on the command line therefore matters.
- `clear(name)` — removes a type's definition entirely from the map.
- `add_defaults()` — loads `default_types::DEFAULT_TYPES`, a
  `&[(&[&str], &[&str])]` of (names, globs) pairs, lexicographically sorted
  and manually curated.

`build()` (`types.rs:322`) does the real compilation: it walks
`self.selections` *in the order they were added*, resolves each to its
`FileTypeDef`, and appends its globs to a `GlobSetBuilder`, recording
`glob_to_selection` entries as it goes. `has_selected` is true iff any
selection is a non-negated `Select`. Because `Types::matched` takes the
*last* matching glob index from `GlobSet::matches_into`, and glob index order
follows selection order, **later `-t`/`-T` flags on the command line take
precedence over earlier ones when their globs overlap the same file name**.

## Matching semantics

`Types::matched(path, is_dir)` (`types.rs:261`) returns `Match<Glob<'_>>`:

- Directories are never matched — `is_dir` short-circuits to `Match::None`.
  Type filters can only ever affect regular file selection, never directory
  pruning during the walk.
- Only the file *name* (`pathutil::file_name`) is tested, not the full path
  or any parent directory component.
- If a path has no file name and any type is `Select`-ed, it's `Ignore`d;
  otherwise `None`.
- Otherwise the globs are matched against the name; the highest-precedence
  match (last index) decides `Whitelist` (from a `Select`) or `Ignore` (from
  a `Negate`).
- If nothing matched at all: `Ignore` if `has_selected` (whitelist mode — only
  recognized types pass), else `None` (no opinion).

## Integration into the walker

`ignore::dir::IgnoreBuilder::types()` stores an `Arc<Types>` on the per-
directory `Ignore` state; `WalkBuilder::types()` (`walk.rs:702`) is the public
entry point. Inside `Ignore::matched_dir_entry`/`matched` (`dir.rs:399`),
type-matching is checked *after* `-g/--glob` overrides and ignore-file rules:
overrides return immediately either way; ignore-file `Ignore` results return
immediately, but a `Whitelist` from ignore files is only remembered, not
returned; types are checked last with the same short-circuit-on-ignore,
remember-on-whitelist pattern, and the final verdict is whichever whitelist
survived (or `None`). This is the documented precedence: `--glob` beats
gitignore rules beats `--type`.

## CLI wiring and contributor notes

`crates/core/flags/defs.rs` defines `Type`, `TypeAdd`, `TypeClear`, `TypeNot`,
`TypeList` as `Flag` impls that each push a `TypeChange` (`Select`, `Add`,
`Clear`, `Negate`) onto `LowArgs::type_changes: Vec<TypeChange>` — a flat,
order-preserving log of everything the user typed. `hiargs::types()`
(`hiargs.rs:1177`) replays that log against a fresh `TypesBuilder::new()` (`add_defaults()` first,
then each `TypeChange` in order) and calls `build()`. Because both
`TypesBuilder` and the CLI preserve command-line order end to end, a
contributor adding a new flag or changing evaluation order must keep that
property — reordering `type_changes` before replay, or building selections
out of order, changes which type wins on overlapping globs.

When adding a built-in type, edit `default_types.rs` only: keep entries
lexicographically sorted and wrapped near 79 columns (per the file's own
doc comment), and prefer extending an existing name array (e.g. `["bat",
"batch"]`) over duplicating globs under two separate type names. Tests for
matching/precedence/error behavior live inline in `types.rs`'s `#[cfg(test)]
mod tests`, using the `matched!` macro; add cases there for new selection or
precedence behavior rather than only relying on the CLI-level integration
tests under `tests/`.
"}
